questions.q: What is an Operator in Airflow?
options: A Python class that acts as a template for one kind of work, like running Python code or a shell command
A person who administers the Airflow server
A SQL keyword used inside DAG files
A synonym for a DAG run
questions.explain: An Operator is a reusable template class — you instantiate it with the specifics of your situation rather than writing the underlying logic yourself.

questions.q: What is the difference between an Operator and a Task?
options: An Operator is the class (e.g. BashOperator); a Task is one instantiation of it inside a DAG, with its own task_id and history
They are exactly the same thing, just different names
A Task is the class; an Operator is one instantiation of it
An Operator can only be used once per Airflow installation
questions.explain: The Operator is reusable template code; a Task is a specific, named instance of that template within a particular DAG.

questions.q: In the BashOperator example from this lesson, what is the one thing you had to supply to make it work?
options: The bash_command to run, plus a task_id
A full custom Python implementation of how to run shell commands
Nothing — BashOperator requires zero arguments
A database connection string
questions.explain: BashOperator already knows how to execute a shell command and report status — you just supply which command to run and a task_id.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what do PythonOperator and BashOperator each handle?
options: PythonOperator wraps any Python callable; BashOperator wraps a shell command
Both only work with SQL queries
PythonOperator is for shell commands, BashOperator is for Python functions
They are interchangeable with no functional difference
questions.explain: PythonOperator runs a Python callable as a task; BashOperator runs a shell command as a task — each covered in full next chapter.

questions.q: What is a "provider operator," and why would you use one instead of custom code?
options: An Operator purpose-built for a specific external system (like Snowflake or S3) that already knows how to authenticate and communicate with it correctly
A deprecated feature no longer supported in current Airflow
An operator that only works inside Airflow's own test suite
A synonym for PythonOperator
questions.explain: Provider operators save you from writing custom connection and authentication code by hand for well-known external systems.
